message.content:
Lions (family Felidae, order Carnivora) and zebras (genus Equus, order Perissodactyla) share a most recent common ancestor that belongs to the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
This ancestor was a small, probably insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly **100–120 million years ago**, during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene. It represents the last common ancestor of the two lineages that later gave rise to modern carnivorans (including cats, dogs, bears, etc.) and perissodactyls (horses, rhinos, tapirs).
